title: Hua, Deadly Betrothed (新娘阿花) - Location, Tactics & Rewards
description: Hua, Deadly Betrothed (新娘阿花) in Phantom Blade Zero - where she waits beneath the Valley Sha-Chi Tower, how to read her grab and lily tells, what patch 1.0302256 changed, and the Scarlet Wraithblade she drops.
keyword: Hua, Deadly Betrothed (新娘阿花) phantom blade zero boss

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Flesh Lily Fields, below the Valley Sha-Chi Tower in Weeping Creek Valley

facts.label: Optional
facts.value: Yes - but required for Yu'er's Flesh Lily request and the Scarlet Wraithblade

facts.label: Drops
facts.value: Scarlet Wraithblade, plus the Twin Flesh Lilies for the quest

facts.label: Unblockable move
facts.value: A grab - dodge only, and the window is late

facts.label: Patch 1.0302256
facts.value: Grab frequency reduced on Wayfarer and Pathbreaker only

facts.label: Weak to
facts.value: No elemental system - counter by colour, not by damage type

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Hua, Deadly Betrothed (新娘阿花) is an optional boss in Weeping Creek Valley, fought in a field of red spider lilies under the first Sha-Chi Tower. Nothing in the main story requires her - but two things make her hard to skip: she drops the Scarlet Wraithblade, and she is the fight that closes Yu'er's Flesh Lily request, which feeds into the true ending route.

She is also the fight S-GAME chose to tune first. Patch 1.0302256 on 4 November reduced how often she uses her grab on the two lower difficulties, which tells you exactly where players were getting stuck: not on her damage, but on a single unblockable move with a late dodge window, in an arena that is trying to kill you at the same time.

sections.title: Where to Find Hua
sections.content:
From the Valley Sha-Chi Tower bell in Weeping Creek Valley, take the path under the tower rather than climbing it. That route drops into the lily field; walking in triggers her cutscene immediately, with no confirmation prompt and no way back out until the fight resolves. Set your weapons, Phantom Edge and consumables before you approach - not while standing in the flowers.

If you are already working Yu'er's questline, you will arrive here by following the Flesh Lily request rather than by looking for a boss. That is the normal route; there is no quest marker pointing at the arena itself.

sections.title: What Patch 1.0302256 Changed
sections.content:
The 4 November patch is specific and narrow: Hua uses her grab attacks less often on Wayfarer (入阵者) and Pathbreaker (破局者), and S-GAME states plainly that other difficulty settings are unaffected. Hellwalker and 66 Days keep the original frequency, so advice written in the first week of November still applies there in full.

What the patch did not do: it did not reduce the grab's damage, its range, or change how late you have to dodge. It reduced how often the situation arises. If you were dying to the grab itself rather than to its frequency, the fix is still on your side - see the move list below.

Two consequences worth knowing. Players who beat her before 4 November on Wayfarer or Pathbreaker beat the harder version, so "it took me nine tries" and "it took me three" can both be true of the same fight. And because the patch also cut PC start-up shader compilation, retrying her repeatedly no longer costs a recompile each relaunch.

sections.title: Tells, Not Weaknesses
sections.content:
There is no weakness table for this fight because there is no damage-type system to fill one in: nothing here resists, absorbs or is immune to anything, and a chart that says otherwise has been inferred from how the boss looks. Read the fight by attack colour instead - red must be dodged, blue must be deflected, purple means it has just parried you and a counter is already coming. The full explanation is on the combat system.

It is optional, which is why it can be left until the Sha-Chi pool and the Phantom Edge roster are deeper.

sections.title: How to Beat Hua, Deadly Betrothed
sections.content:
The shape of the fight

Treat her as one continuous phase rather than a scripted sequence. She pressures with long sword strings, mixes in the grab, and uses the lilies to deny floor space. The fight is won by converting her strings into posture damage instead of trading hits.

1. Parry the strings, do not trade with them

Her sweeping combinations hit hard but are largely deflectable, and consecutive deflects are the fastest route to breaking her Sha-Chi. Two or three clean deflections in a row open the first real damage window; blocking the same string instead costs you the posture race and leaves you in range for the grab.

2. Dodge the grab on commitment, not on reaction to the red

The grab is unblockable and the dodge window is late. Reacting to the red flash alone tends to dodge too early. Watch for the moment she commits - the step-in before the reach - and dodge then. If you cannot read it yet, stay out of grab range entirely between damage windows rather than trying to parry your way out.

3. Move out of the lilies before they detonate

The bloom is the tell, the detonation is delayed. Do not fight her on top of a bloomed flower to finish a combo; the exchange you win is smaller than the health bar you lose. Walk the arena in a shallow arc so you are never standing in the field you just fought through.

4. Bank your burst for the posture break

Heavy attacks and weapon skills cost Sha-Chi, so spend them when her meter breaks, not to open the fight. A weapon that closes distance helps here - the arena is small and she retreats into the lilies between strings.

5. If you only want the quest, lower the difficulty

There is no difficulty trophy in this game, and difficulty can be changed freely. Wayfarer exists; her grab is now less frequent there. Beating her on Wayfarer still counts for the Flesh Lily request and still drops the Scarlet Wraithblade.

sections.title: Rewards
sections.content:
• Scarlet Wraithblade - her weapon, and the reason many players fight her at all
  • Twin Flesh Lilies - the quest item Yu'er's Flesh Lily request needs; the fight and the fetch are the same trip
  • Trophy: Scarlet Wraithblade (Bronze), awarded on the kill regardless of difficulty

sections.title: Status
sections.content: No. 5 of 60 in the progression order, in Prologue & Weeping Creek Valley. Before it: Peng Meng, the Axemaster (斧老大 彭猛). After it: Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet. The roster by region is on the boss list, and the fights that can be lost by leaving a region early are on the order page. Location and drops come from the shipped game; patch 1.0302256 is the most recent change to any boss behaviour and it touched only Hua.
